The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 20-03-2011.

sentences.text: Initially this case was tried by clubbing this case with MVC No.3532/2011 and 3534/2011 and disposed off by common judgment dated 18-10-2012.

Thereafter as per the order of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.1952/2013 (MV) dated 23-10-2024, remanded only this case to this court by setting aside the earlier judgment only in respect of MVC No.3533/2011.
After giving the opportunity for all the parties, the case is taken for disposal.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 20-03-2011 at about 1.30 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding as a inmate of the Maruthi Omni Car bearing No. KA.51.MA.8197 on Krishnagiri - Vaniyambadi NH 4 road and when he reached near U turn at Natarampalli, at that time the driver of private bus bearing No. TN.49.P.5229 came from Natarampalli towards Kotur and driven the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, suddenly took right turn without giving any indication and dashed against the car in which the petitioner was proceeding and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained severe head injuries.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Christian medical college at Vellore, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and then he was shifted to Narayana Hrudayalaya hospital, Bangalore, wherein also he took treatment as an inpatient.
Petitioner has spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical and travelling expenses.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy, aged about 28 years and he was working as a office assistant at Infosys Limited and earning Rs.8,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3. Inspite of service of notice respondent No.1- owner of offending vehicle has not appeared before the court, hence placed Exparte.
After service of summons, respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by denying the occupation and income of the petitioner.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident and involvement of the offending bus in the alleged accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is fanciful, speculative, exorbitant and highly disproportionate.
Further contended that there is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 20-03-2011 at about 1.30 p.m when the petitioner was traveling in Maruthi Omni Car near U turn at Natarampalli on Krishnagiri - Vaniyambadi, NH 4 road, at that time, one Private bus bearing No.

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ? If so, at what rate and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner in common trial along with MVC No.3532/2011 and 3534/2011 examined himself as P.W.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.18 to 21.
Further the senior executive in MRD of Narayana Hrudalaya general hospital is examined as PW.4 and got marked the documents at Ex.P26 to P28.
The MRO of Christian Medical college is examined as PW.5 senior accountant in CMC hospital, Vellore is examined as PW.6 and got marked the documents at Ex.P29 to P33.
Inspite of sufficient opportunity respondents have not lead any evidence.
6. I have heard the arguments and perused the materials that are available on record.

8. That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.2.
The crime records and police documents were produced by the petitioner of MVC No.3532/2021 in common trial.
In support of his case, the true copies of FIR, complaint, sketch and final report and their translation copies were also produced in a common trial in earlier stage.

9. On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of first information given by one Prasannakumar by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Bus bearing No.
TN.49.P.5229.
After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P2 spot mahazar and Ex.P3 spot sketch were conducted.
On perusal of Ex.P3 spot mahazar, the accident spot is in the right side portion of the road.

It is alleged that the driver of the bus bearing No.TN-49-P-5229 by driving his bus in rash and negligent manner suddenly took right turn and hit the left side of the car in which the petitioner was proceeding.
The rough sketch marked at Ex.P3 clearly evidentiates that the accident spot is near to the U turn.

The Ex.P.27 are the IMV reports wherein the car bearing No.KA-51- MA-8197 has got major damages in front side and front left side whereas the offending bus bearing No.TN-49-P- 5229 has got damages in its right hand side bumper and indicator.

sentences.text: Thereby it is established that the offending bus without observing the moving vehicles in the right side has taken sudden right and thereby dashed against the left side front portion of the car in which the petitioner was proceeding.
Thus, by producing these documents the petitioner prima-facie establishes the negligence of the driver of the bus.
The contents of Ex.P2 & 3 supported the case of the petitioner to prove the alleged negligence of the driver of the Bus bearing No. TN.49.P.5229.
If the driver of Bus bearing No. TN.49.P.5229 was not taken the sudden right turn his bus was not going to be dash against the left side of the car.

10. Ex.P8 charge sheet is also came to be filed on against the driver of the Bus bearing No.
TN.49.P.5229, for the offences punishable U/Sec.279, 337, 338 and 304(a) of IPC and the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of the Bus bearing No. TN.49.P.5229.
No other grounds are made out by the respondents to show the contributory negligence from the petitioner.
11. The respondent No.2 has filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability.
But both the respondents have not lead any evidence to rebut the case of the petitioner.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of the Bus bearing No. TN.49.P.5229.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Bus bearing No.
TN.49.P.5229.
12.
The first respondent who is the owner of the offending vehicle does not chosen to deny the allegation of the rash and negligence driving.
The respondent no.2 even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.
The respondent No.1 & 2 even after sufficient opportunity have not lead any evidence to disprove the contents of these documents.
The charge sheet is came to be filed on the the driver of the Bus bearing No. TN.49.P.5229 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337, 338 & 304(a) of IPC.

Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

15. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by denying their liability and alleged negligence, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.
16. The contents of Ex.P2 spot mahazar and Ex.P3 spot sketch helped the petitioner to prove his case.

In this context by considering the contents of documents produced by the petitioner this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.
17. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 20-03-2011 which is caused by the driver of the Bus bearing No. TN.49.P.5229 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
18.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
19. The petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P18.

On perusal of the same it reveals that the petitioner was admitted to the Narayana Hrudayalaya hospital, Bangalore from 03-04-2011 to 11-04-2011 and also at Christian Medical College from 20-03-2011 to 03-04-2011 and has sustained moderate head injury, right anterior temporal contusion and left frontal contusion pneumocephalus.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated him at the time of accident.
Without the evidence of doctor, it is not possible to believe that, the petitioner has sustained disability due to grievous injuries.

20. According to the petitioner he was working as a office Assistant at Infosys Limited and earning Rs.8,000/- p.m.
21.

While determining the compensation this court has to look into the pain and sufferings, medical expenses, diet, food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges and loss of amenities and enjoyment of life that the PW-1 has suffered, which are discussed herein below:
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 28 years.

sentences.text: As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P18 the petitioner was admitted to the Narayana Hrudayalaya hospital, Bangalore from 03-04-2011 to 11-04-2011 and also at Christian Medical College from 20-03-2011 to 03-04-2011 and has sustained moderate head injury, right anterior temporal contusion and left frontal contusion pneumocephalus.
By considering the nature of the injuries and the period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.30,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P21 amounting to Rs.3,56,357/-.
These bills are supported with medical prescriptions which are also marked at Ex.P21.
As these bills are disputed the petitioner examined PW.4 to PW.6.
PW.4 is the senior executive and MRD, Narayana Hrudayalaya hospital who produced Ex.P27 letter dated 30.01.2025 and Ex.P28 copies of inpatient case details.
As per Ex.P27 the original records are destroyed and the copies of the medical records were maintained in digital format.
Ex. P28 are the print out of the digitalized medical records of the petitioner.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P28 the petitioner admitted to Narayana Hrudayala hospital on 03.04.2011 and discharged on 11.04.2021.
He admitted with the alleged history of RTA and had right anterior temporal and left frontal contusion along with chest injury.
The documents available in the Ex.P28 shows the day to day treatment given to the petitioner.
Further the PW.5 is a medical record officer of Christian Medical College, Vellur who produced copies of inpatient case details as Ex.P29 and true copies of X-ray, CT scan and lab reports as Ex.P30.

The documents available at Ex.P29 discloses that the petitioner admitted to their hospital on 20.03.2011 and discharged on 03.04.2011 and also the day to day treatment taken by the petitioner during his admission in the said hospital.
Very particularly the CT scan report marked at Ex.P30 discloses the injuries caused on the head of the petitioner.

PW.6 is the senior accountant in CMC hospital who produced Ex.P32 statement of account and Ex.P33 consolidated receipt with inpatient bill which helped the petitioner to show the payment made towards his treatment in the Christian Medical College, Vellur.
The Ex.P27 to P33 helped the petitioner to support the medical bills produced by him at Ex.P21.
No grounds are made out to doubt the bills after examining the PW.4 to PW.6.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same to i.e., Rs.3,56,400/-.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitle for the same.

(C) TOWARDS DIET, FOOD, NOURISHMENT, ATTENDANT AND CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

sentences.text: As already observed the Ex.P-18, makes it amply clear that the petitioner underwent treatment for the injuries sustained by him.
During the said period the petitioner might have taken assistance from others and taken diet food.
On consideration of the injuries sustained by the petitioner this Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and proper to award an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
(D) TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNING CAPACITY ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
It is necessary to note that the loss of future earning capacity cannot be presumed and has to be proved with cogent evidence.

But interestingly the petitioner though claims that he is unable to do any work and has become permanently disabled he has not put in any efforts to prove the disability by examining the doctor, who treated him.
In fact he has not even produced the disability certificate issued by competent authority.
In the absence of any such material piece of evidence, it is very difficult for this Court to assess the disability and thereby assess the loss of earning capacity due to disability.
The petitioner has also admitted in his cross examination that still he is working at Infosys as Admin Assistant and earning Rs.60,000/- p.m.
This makes it clear that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability.

Hence, this court has no option but to hold that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability which has resulted in reduction of his salary/pension and hence he is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
(E) TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner in his cross examination has stated that due to the accidental injuries he could not attend his work from 20-03-2011 to 16-08-2011 and salary was not paid during these days.
But in order to prove the same the petitioner has not produced any documents.
The Ex.P.19 salary slip shows that petitioner was earning Rs.8852/- per month after the accident.
But the petitioner has not produced any documents to show that his salary was deducted after the accident as he was unable to attend office.
No evidence is placed by the petitioner by showing that he has availed the leaves which in turn he has lost his salary or earned leaves.

The petitioner has not made out any evidence or grounds to hold that she sustained the loss of income during the laid down period hence, in the absence of any evidence, petitioner is not entitled for any amount under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
(F) TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES AND ENJOYMENT OF LIFE:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award him a reasonable sum of Rs.25,000/- under this head.

In the written statement of the respondent No.2- insurance company stated that the liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
No other grounds are made out to show the violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1 - owner.
Hence, the said defence of the respondent No.2 insurance company cannot be acceptable.
Accordingly, the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the liability of respondent No.1 owner and they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
